translations.text: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job. That man was truthful, blameless, righteous, and God-fearing, keeping away from every evil and sinful deed.
He had seven sons and three daughters.

His livestock consisted of seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, and five hundred grazing female donkeys. He had very many servants and extensive operations throughout the land. That man was more distinguished than all the people of the East.
His sons would gather together and hold feasts with one another every day, taking their three sisters with them to eat and drink with them.

When the days of feasting came to an end, Job would send for them and purify them. Rising early in the morning, he would offer sacrifices for them according to their number, and one bull for sins on behalf of their children. For Job said, “Perhaps my children have thought evil of God in their minds.” Job did this throughout all their days.
One day, the angels of God came to stand before the Lord. Satan also came among them, having wandered about the earth and traveled through it.
The Lord said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered the Lord, “I have come from traveling through the earth and wandering beneath the heavens.”
The Lord said to him, “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth, a blameless, truthful, God-fearing man who keeps away from every evil deed.”
Satan answered and said to the Lord, “Does Job worship the Lord for nothing?”
“Have you not fortified everything outside his house and everything within it, and all that surrounds him? You have blessed the work of his hands and multiplied his livestock throughout the land.
But please, stretch out your hand and strike all his possessions, and he will surely curse you to your face.”
Then the Lord said to Satan, “Look, I give all his possessions into your hands, but do not touch him.” And Satan went out from the Lord’s presence.
One day, Job’s sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house.
A messenger came to Job and said to him, “The teams of oxen were plowing, and the female donkeys were grazing beside them,
when raiders came and carried them off, and killed the servants with the sword. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another messenger came to Job and said, “Fire fell from heaven and burned the flocks, and likewise consumed the shepherds. I alone was left and came to tell you.”

While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, “Raiders attacked us in three bands, surrounded the camels, and carried them off. They killed the servants with the sword. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, “While your sons and daughters were eating and drinking at their eldest brother’s house,
suddenly a great wind came from the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house. The house fell on your children, and they died. I alone escaped and came to tell you.”
Then Job got up, tore his clothes, cut off the hair of his head, and fell to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
And he said, “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked I will return there.”
“The Lord gave, and the Lord took away. As it pleased the Lord, so it happened. Blessed be the name of the Lord.”
In all these calamities that befell him, Job did not sin before the Lord or attribute folly to God.
One day, the angels of God came to stand before God. Satan also came among them to stand with them before the Lord.
The Lord said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan said before the Lord, “I have come from roaming beneath the heavens and traveling everywhere.”

And the Lord said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant Job? There is no one like him on earth, a truthful, blameless, God-fearing man who keeps away from all evil. He still remains innocent, and you spoke without cause to have his possessions destroyed.”
Satan answered the Lord again, “Skin for skin! A man will give up everything he has for his own life.”
“Otherwise, please stretch out your hand and strike his bones and his flesh, and see whether he will not bless you to your face.”
And the Lord said to Satan, “Look, I hand him over to you, but you must spare his life.”
And Satan went out from the Lord’s presence and struck Job with terrible sores from his feet to his head.
He took a potsherd and scraped away the pus, and he sat on a dung heap outside the city.

After a long time had passed, his wife said to him, “How long will you endure and say, ‘Look, I will wait a little longer, hoping for my deliverance’? See, your memory has perished from the earth—your sons and daughters, the pains and birth pangs of my womb, for whom I labored in suffering for nothing. You yourself sit in the filth of worms, spending the night out in the open, while I wander, driven from house to house and from place to place, waiting for the sun to set so that I may rest from my hardships and the pains that now surround me. Come, say something to the Lord and die!”

He looked at her and said, “You have spoken like one of the foolish women. If we have received good things from the Lord’s hand, should we not endure these evils?” In all these things that happened to him, Job did not sin with his lips before the Lord, nor did he attribute folly to God.

When his three friends heard about all the calamities that had befallen him, they came to him, each from his own country: Eliphaz, king of the Temanites; Bildad, ruler of the Shuhites; and Zophar, king of the Minaeans. They came together to comfort and console him.
When they saw him from a distance, they did not recognize him. They cried aloud and wept, and each tore his robe and scattered dust over their heads, looking up toward heaven.
They sat around him on the ground for seven days and seven nights, and none of them spoke a word to him, because they saw that his afflictions were unbearable and exceedingly great.
After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed his day
and said:
“May the day on which I was born perish, and the night on which they said, ‘Look, a boy!’
May that night become dark. May the Lord above not seek it out, and may no light come upon it.
May darkness and the shadow of death take hold of it; may a cloud come upon it.
May that day and night be cursed, and may darkness carry it away. May it not be among the days of the year or be counted among the days of the months.
Instead, may that night be filled with pain, and may no joy or gladness come upon it.
Let the one who is to curse that day curse it, the one who is indeed to subdue the great dragon by force.
Let the stars of that night grow dark; let it wait and not come into the light, and let it not see the morning star rising.
For it did not close the doors of my mother’s womb, which might have kept pain from my eyes.
Why did I not die in the womb? Why did I come out of the womb and not perish immediately there?
Why did [?] meet me, or why did I suck my mother’s breasts?
For now I would be lying still, and I would be asleep and at rest,
with kings and counselors of the earth who took pride in their swords,
or with princes who had much gold and filled their houses with silver,
or like a miscarried child that comes out of its mother’s womb, or like infants who never saw the light.
There the wicked who kindled the fury of anger, there those whose bodies were worn out, came to rest.
The everlasting ones are together, those who did not hear the taskmaster’s voice.
The small and the great are there, and the servant has no fear of his master.
But why is light given to embittered souls, and life to those whose spirits are in pain?
They long for death but do not attain it; they dig for it as for treasures.
And they are filled with joy if they find death.
There is rest for a man whose way has been hidden from him, because God has shut him in.
Before my food, my groaning came with tears, and I am oppressed by fear.
For the terror I dreaded came upon me, and what I feared happened to me.
I had no peace, no quiet, no rest, because wrath came upon me.
Eliphaz the Temanite speaks again in reply.
Have your words often been spoken with weariness? And who can endure the force of your words?
For you instructed many and strengthened weak hands.
You raised up the sick with your words and clothed faltering knees with courage.
And now pains have come upon you, yet you have become agitated.
Is not your fear foolishness, as are your anxiety and the innocence of your way?
Now remember: who ever perished while holy? Or were the upright ever torn out by the roots?
As I have seen, those who plow what is wrong and sow it will reap pain from it.
At the Lord’s command they will perish; by the breath of his wrath they will be destroyed.
The lion’s strength, the lioness’s roar, and the dragons’ pride have been extinguished.
The ant-lion perished for lack of food; the lion’s cubs abandoned one another.
If there had still been a true word in your speech, none of these evils would have happened to you. Will my ear not then receive wondrous things from him?
Terrors and rumblings in the night brought fear upon people.
Trembling and terror came upon me and shook my bones violently.
And a wind came upon my face; my hair and flesh shuddered.
I stood still and did not understand; I looked, but there were no forms before my eyes. I heard only air and a rustling.
But now, can a person be holy before the Lord, or a man be blameless in his deeds?
If he does not trust his servants and has found some fault even in his angels,
then he struck down those who live in houses of clay—we ourselves being made of that same clay—like a moth.
From morning to evening they cease to exist; because they could not help themselves, they perished.
He blew upon them, and they dried up; they perished because there was no wisdom in them.
Now, please call out: will anyone answer you? Or will you see any of the holy angels?
For anger kills the fool, and jealousy puts the misguided person to death.
Indeed, I have seen fools putting down roots, but their dwellings were suddenly struck down.
Let their children be far from deliverance; let them be mistreated at the gates of the wicked, with no one to rescue them.
For the righteous will eat what they gathered. Let them not escape their troubles; their strength will be drained away.
For hardship does not come out of the earth, nor do pains sprout from the mountains.
Rather, a human being is born to toil, while young eagles fly to the heights.
But I will seek the Lord and call upon the Lord, the ruler of all,
Who does great and unsearchable things, glorious things and wondrous works beyond number.
who gives rain upon the earth and sends water beneath the heavens,
who raises the lowly to the heights and sets the lost upright,
and overturns the plans of the crafty, so that their hands will not accomplish what is true,
who catches the wise in their cleverness and has confounded the plans of schemers.
Darkness will meet them by day, and at noon they will grope about as though it were night. They will perish in war.
And the poor person will be saved from the hand of the powerful.
There will be hope for the weak, and the mouth of the unjust will be shut.
Blessed is the person whom the Lord has rebuked. Do not reject the discipline of the Almighty.
For he causes pain and then restores again; he struck, and his hands healed.
Six times he will rescue you from distress, and the seventh time no evil will come near you.
In famine he will rescue you from death; in war he will free you from the power of iron.
He will hide you from the torments of the tongue, and you will not fear the evils coming upon you.
You will scorn the unjust and the lawless; you will not fear wild beasts.
For your covenant will be with the stones of the field, and the wild beasts will be at peace with you.
Then you will know that your house is at peace, and that life in your home will not go wrong.
And you will know that your offspring are many, and your children will be like the plants of the field.
And you will go to the grave like ripe wheat harvested in its season, or like a heap on the threshing floor gathered in its season.
Look, we have examined this in this way; this is what we have heard. But know for yourself what you have done.
Job speaks again.
If only someone would weigh my anger and put my pain together with it on the scales!
It would be heavier than the sand of the sea; therefore my words are senseless.
For the Lord's arrows are in my body, and his wrath sucks my blood. Whenever I begin to speak, they torment me.
Now, would a wild donkey bray for no reason, unless it were seeking food? Or would an ox bellow at the manger when it has food?
Can bread be eaten without salt, or is there any flavor in empty words?
My soul cannot endure this, for I see my food with pus, like the smell of a lion.
If only he would grant it, and my requests would come to me, and the Lord would give me what I hope for!
The Lord has begun to wound me, but let him not kill me altogether.
May my city be my grave, upon whose walls I used to walk. I will not spare it, for I will not falsify the words of my holy God.
For what strength do I have to endure, or what time remains for my soul to be at peace?
Is my strength the strength of rocks, or is my flesh bronze? Or did I not trust in him?
Now my help has been driven away from me, and mercy has withdrawn from me; the Lord’s care has passed me by.
Those close to me paid no attention to me.
Like a dwindling stream and like waves, they passed over me.
Those who trembled before me have now come against me.
Like snow or frozen ice that melts when warmth arrives, so that no one can recognize what it was,
so I too have been abandoned by everyone; I have perished and become destitute.
Look at the roads of the people of Tema, you who look toward the paths of Sheba.
And those who put their hope in cities and possessions will be ashamed.
So you too now come against me without mercy; you look at my wounds and are afraid.
Now, did I ask anything of you?
Or would I need your strength to save me from enemies or rescue me from the hands of the powerful?
Teach me, and I will be silent; if I have gone astray in anything, make me understand.
But then a truthful man's words are worthless, for I am not asking you for strength.
The rebukes in your words will not silence me, nor will I heed the sound of your words.
But you have risen against me as against an orphan, and you have mocked your friend.
But now, looking into your faces, I will not lie. Sit down, and let there be no injustice in the judgment.
And again, pay attention to justice.
For there is no injustice on my tongue, or does my throat not ponder wisdom?
Is not a person's life on earth like a trial, and his life like the daily wages of a hired worker?
Or like a slave afraid of his master and hiding in the shade, or like a hired worker waiting for his wages.
Likewise, I have waited through empty months, and painful nights have been given to me.
If I lie down, I say, “When will it be day?” And if I rise, I say again, “When will it be evening?” I am filled with pain from evening until morning.
My flesh is soaked in the filth of worms. I have worn down clods of earth to scrape off the pus.
My life is lighter than words, and it has perished in the emptiness of hope.
Remember that my life is a breath, and my eye will not again see good.
The eye of one who sees me will no longer look upon me. Your eyes will be upon me, and I will be no more.
Like a cloud wiped away from the heavens—for if a person goes down to Hades,
he will never come up again or return to his house, and his place will no longer recognize him.
From now on I will no longer restrain my mouth. I will speak while I am in sorrow; in my distress I will reveal the bitterness of my soul.
Am I a sea or a sea monster, that you have set a guard over me?
I said, “My bed will comfort me; I will put my words behind me on my couch.”
You terrify me with dreams and strike me with visions.
You draw the spirit out of my soul, my breath out of my body, and my life out of death.
For I will not live forever, even if I am patient. Leave me alone, for my life is empty.
For what is a human being, that you have made him great, or that you should give him your attention,
or visit him until morning and judge him when he is at rest?
How long will you refuse to leave me alone and give me no relief, until I swallow my saliva in pain?
For if I have sinned, what can I do to you, who know people's thoughts? Why have you made me your adversary, so that I am a burden to you?
And why have you not forgotten my lawlessness and cleansed my sins? Now, behold, I will soon return to the earth and be no more.
Again Bildad the Shuhite says in reply:
“How long will you speak these things, and a spirit of boasting be in your mouth?”
Will the Lord judge unjustly, or will the one who made everything pervert justice?
If your children sinned before him, he delivered them into the power of their own lawlessness.
But you, seek the Lord Almighty early with prayers.
If you are pure and truthful, he will hear your prayers and restore to you a dwelling of righteousness.
Your beginnings will be small, but your latter days will be boundless.
But please ask the earliest generation, and investigate according to the families of the fathers.
For we are but of yesterday and know nothing, because our lives on earth are a shadow.
Will not those very people teach you and tell you, and bring forth words from their hearts?
Does papyrus grow green without water, or does a rush grow tall without drinking?
While it is still there on its roots, will it not be cut down before all the plants have drunk? If it is not watered, will it not dry up?
Such will be the end of all who forget the Lord, for the hope of the ungodly will perish.
His house will be deserted; his dwelling will pass away like a spider’s web.
Even if he makes his house firm, may it not stand; when he lays his hand on it, may it not hold firm.
For it is moist beneath the sun, and its shoot will come forth from its decay.
It will lie on a heap of stones and stand among small stones. If it is swallowed up, the place will deny it.
Have you not seen such a thing?
For such is the destruction of the ungodly, and another will sprout from the earth.
For the Lord does not reject the innocent; he will not accept any offering of the ungodly.
The mouths of the upright will be filled with laughter, and their lips with thanksgiving.
Their enemies will be clothed with shame, and the dwellings of the ungodly will no longer exist.
Job spoke again in reply:
I truly know that this is so, for how can a person be righteous before God?
For if he wished to dispute with him, he would not listen to him, for he would not answer even one word out of a thousand.
For he is wise in mind, powerful and great. Who has hardened himself against him and remained untroubled?
He wears down the mountains, and they do not know it; he overturns them in anger.
He shakes what is beneath heaven from its foundations, and its pillars tremble.
He commands the sun, and it does not rise; he seals up the stars.
Who alone stretched out the heavens and walks upon the sea as upon a floor.
Who made the Pleiades, the Evening Star, the Great Bear, and the storehouses of the south.
Who does great, unsearchable, glorious, and wonderful things beyond number.
If he passes over me, I will not see him; and if he passes beside me, even then I will not know it.
And if he destroys, who will turn him back? Or who will say to him, “What have you done?”
For he turned away from anger, and the sea monsters beneath the heavens trembled before him.
If only he would listen to me and vindicate my words!
Even if I am righteous, he will not listen to me, and I will plead for his judgment.
And if I call and he answers, I do not believe that he has actually heard me.
He destroys me with a cloud; many are the wounds he has inflicted on me without cause.
He does not let me rest, for he has filled me with bitterness.
For he is mighty and uses force. Who, then, could stand against him in judgment?
Even if I am righteous, my mouth will declare me wicked; and if I am blameless, I will be found perverse.
For if I have been wicked in my soul, I do not know, except that my life is being taken from me.
Therefore I said that anger destroys the great and the mighty.
For the wicked will perish by a terrible death, but the righteous are mocked, for they are handed over into the hands of the ungodly.
He will cover the faces of its judges. And if it is not he, who is it?
But my days are swifter than a courier; they fled and were seen no more.
Or is there any trace of the path of ships, or of an eagle flying in search of food?
If I say, “I will speak,” I forget; with my face cast down, I groan.
I tremble in all my limbs, for I know that you will not leave me blameless.
Since I was wicked, why did I not die?
If I wash myself by hand and cleanse myself with clean hands.
He plunged me into deep filth; my own garment made me abhorrent.
For you are not a man like me, with whom I could contend if we came together for judgment.
But if only there were a mediator who would rebuke and hear both of us.
Let him take his rod away from me, and let his terror not frighten me.
And let me not be afraid, but let me speak. [?] I do not know it to be so, being weary in my soul.
With groaning I will bring my words to him; I will speak in the bitterness of my grieving soul.
And I will say, “Lord, do not teach me to act wickedly. Why have you judged me this way?
Or does it seem good to you that I should be unjust, since you have rejected the work of your hands and paid attention to the plans of the wicked?
Do you look as a man looks, or see as a human being sees?
Or are your years like those of a man,
that you have searched again for my lawlessness and examined my sins?
You know that I have not acted wickedly, but who can rescue me from your hands?
Your hands made me and formed me, and then you turned and struck me.
Remember that you formed me from clay. Will you turn me back into earth again?
Did you not milk me like milk and curdle me like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh; you brought me forth with bones and sinews.
You bestowed life and mercy on me; your care preserved my spirit.
You hold all these things within yourself. I know that you can do everything, and nothing is beyond your strength.
Even if I sin, you watch over me, and you have not made me free from lawlessness.
If I act wickedly, woe to me! And if I am righteous, I cannot look up, because I am full of disgrace.
I am hunted like a lion for slaughter. Again and again you destroy me cruelly.
You renew my afflictions against me. With great anger you have laid your hand on me and brought a raiding band against me.
Why did you bring me out of the womb? Why did I not die there, before any eye had seen me?
I would have been as though I had never existed. Why did I not pass from the womb to the grave?
Is not the time of my life short? Allow me to rest a little,
before I go away, never to return, to a land of darkness and gloom,
to a land of everlasting obscurity, where there is no light and no seeing human life.”
Zophar the Minaean speaks again in reply.
“Whoever speaks much must also listen in turn. Can someone who speaks be justified by words?
Blessed is the short-lived offspring of women. Do not fall into many words, for there is no one to give you an answer.
Do not say, ‘I am holy in my deeds and blameless before the Lord.’
But how might the Lord speak to you and open his lips to you?
Then he would tell you the power of wisdom, for it is twice as great as yours. Then you would know that what has come upon you from the Lord is what you deserve for the sins you committed.
Can you find the Lord’s tracks, or reach the limits of what the Almighty has made?
The heavens are high—what can you do? The depths of the underworld are deep—what can you understand?
The measure of the earth is long; the sea is wide.
And if he overthrows everything, who will say to him, “What have you done?”
He himself knows the deeds of the lawless; he sees their unworthy acts and will not overlook them.
But a man who speaks in vain hides behind words; a man born of woman is like a wild donkey.
But if you have made your heart pure, stretch out your hands to him.
If there is lawlessness in your hand, put it far away from you, and do not let lawlessness dwell in your house.
Then your face will shine like clear water; you will strip away filth and will not be afraid.
And you will forget your hardship like waves that have passed, and you will not be terrified.
Your prayers will be like the morning star; at midday life will dawn for you. You will be confident because your hope remains, and peace will appear to you out of worry and uncertainty.
You will rest quietly, and there will be no one to fight against you.
Many will turn and plead with you; deliverance will fail them.
For their hope is the destruction of their own lives; the eyes of the ungodly will waste away.
Job speaks again in reply.
So you too are human beings, or will wisdom die with you?
My heart is like yours.
For a righteous and blameless man became a laughingstock.
At the appointed time he was destined to be overthrown by a stranger; he saw his houses devastated by lawless men.
Yet let no one who is evil hope to go unpunished. Will not all who provoke the Lord be called to account?
But please ask the four-footed animals whether they will tell you, and the birds of heaven whether they will explain it to you.
Speak to the earth, to see whether it will teach you, or let the fish of the sea tell you.
Who does not know from all these things that the Lord’s hand has made this?
And is not the breath of every living creature and the spirit of every human being in his hand?
For the mind examines words, and the palate tastes food.
Wisdom comes with much time, and understanding with a long life.
Wisdom and strength come from him; counsel and understanding are his.
If he tears down, who will build? And if he shuts someone in, who will open?
If he holds back the waters, he dries up the earth; and if he lets them loose, he destroys it, overturning it.
From him come strength and might; understanding and wisdom are his.
He leads counselors into captivity and has made the judges of the earth foolish.
He seats kings on thrones and puts a belt around their waists.
He sends priests into captivity and has overthrown the mighty of the earth.
He changes the lips of the faithful and has discerned the understanding of elders.
He pours contempt upon rulers and has healed the lowly.
He reveals the depths of darkness and has brought the shadows of death into the light.
He leads nations astray and destroys them; he scatters nations and guides them.
He changes the hearts of the rulers of the earth; he has led them astray on a path they did not know.
They will grope in darkness and not in light; they will wander like a drunken person.
Look, my eye has seen all this, and my ear has heard it.
I know as much as you understand, and I am no more foolish than you.
But I will speak with the Lord; I will argue my case before him, if he wishes.
But to me you are sinful physicians, all of you healers of evils.
May you become silent, and may it be counted as wisdom for you.
Hear the rebuke of my mouth, and listen to the judgment of my lips.
Will you not speak before the Lord and utter deceit in his presence?
Or will you [?], since you have all become judges?
For it is good if he examines you; for if you add to him everything you have done,
he will rebuke you no small amount, even if you show partiality in secret.
Will not his terrors frighten you, and his dread fall upon you?
Your splendors will become like ashes, and your body will be a body of clay.
Be silent so that I may speak and find relief from my anger.
I will take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hand.
If the Mighty One lays his hand upon me—for he has already begun—shall I not speak and argue my case before him?
And this will turn out to be my salvation, for deceit will not come before him.
Listen, listen to my words, for I will speak to you in your hearing.
For see, I have drawn near to my judgment, and I know that I will be shown to be righteous.
For who is my adversary? Let him come, for now I will fall silent and cease to be.
I need two things, and then I will not hide from your presence.
Remove your hand from me, and do not let the fear of you terrify me.
Then call me, and I will listen to you; and if you speak, I will answer you.
How many are my sins and lawless deeds? Teach me how many they are.
Why do you hide from me and regard me as your enemy?
Or will you fear a leaf shaken by the wind, or oppose me as though I were grass driven by the wind?
For you have written bitter things against me and laid upon me the sins of my youth.
You have confined my foot, watched all my deeds, and reached the roots of my feet,
which are like a worn-out wineskin or like moth-eaten rags.
For a man born of woman is short-lived and full of anger,
who blossomed like a flower and withered, fled like a shadow, and does not remain.
Will you not indeed take account of him too? And you have made him enter into judgment before you.
Now who can be clean from impurity? No one at all.
Even if his life on earth lasts only one day, his months are numbered by him; you have set a time, and he will not go beyond it.
Turn away from him so that he may rest and find relief in his life, like a hired worker.
For there is hope for a tree again: even if it is cut down, it will bloom once more, and its shoots will not fail.
If its root grows old in the earth and its trunk dies in the rock,
at the scent of water it will bloom and produce a crop like a newly planted tree.
But a man dies and is gone; a human being falls and is no more.
For in time the sea dwindles, and rivers become desolate and dry up.
And a man lies down and will not rise. Until the heavens cease to exist, they will not be restored or wake from their sleep.
If only you would keep me in the realm of the dead and hide me until your anger passed, and appoint a time for me when you would remember me!
If a man dies after completing the days of his life, will he live? I will wait until I come into being again.
Then you will call me, and I will answer you. Do not reject the works of your hands.
You have counted my steps; can any of my sins escape you?
You sealed my iniquities in a bag and noted whether I had transgressed unintentionally.
Yet even a mountain that is going to collapse will collapse, and a rock will wear away from its place.
The waters smoothed the stones, and the waters flooded the plains of the solid earth; and you destroyed man's hope.
You drove him away completely, and he departed; you set your face against him and sent him away.
Even if his children become numerous, he does not know; and if they become few, he does not recognize it.
But his flesh suffered pain upon him, and his soul mourned for itself.
Eliphaz the Temanite speaks again in reply.
Will a discerning man answer with spiritual wisdom and fill his belly with suffering,
rebuking with words that are not fitting, with speech that is of no benefit?
Yet you have also cast off fear and brought such words together before the Lord.
You have made yourself guilty through the words of your mouth, and you have not examined the words of the mighty.
Your own mouth will rebuke you, not I; your lips will testify against you.
How, then? Were you born before other people, or were you established before the hills?
Have you heard the Lord's command, or has wisdom come to you?
What do you know that we do not know, or what do you understand that we do not?
Indeed, among us there is one who is old and advanced in days, older than your father.
You have been punished little in comparison with your sins, and you have spoken even more boastfully.
Why has your heart become so bold, or why have your eyes become shameless,
that you have poured out your anger before the Lord and brought such words out of your mouth?
What man has ever been blameless, or who born of a woman will be righteous?
For if he does not trust the holy ones, and the heavens are not pure before him,
how much less a vile and unclean man, who drinks iniquity as though it were a drink!
I will tell you, Job; listen to me. What I have seen, I will tell you:
what the wise say and have not hidden from their fathers.
To them alone the land was given, and no foreigner came among them.
The whole life of the ungodly is full of anxieties; a fixed number of years is given to the mighty.
His terror is in his ears; when he thinks he is at peace, his destruction will come.
Let him not believe that he will return from darkness, for he has already been consigned to the hands of iron.
He has been appointed as food for vultures; he knows in his mind that destruction awaits him.
The dark day will terrify him; anguish and distress will come upon him like a commander fallen in the front ranks.
For he raised his hands against the Lord and rebelled before the Lord Almighty.
He charged at him arrogantly, with his thick shield.
For he covered his face with his fat and made a double edge on his thigh.
He will dwell in ruined cities and enter uninhabited houses. Others will carry away what they prepared.
Let him not grow great, and let his possessions not endure. Let him not cast a shadow on the earth, and let him not escape from darkness.
Let the wind wither his bud; let his flower be shaken off.
Let him not believe that he will find rest; vain things will befall him.
His stump will be struck before its time, and let his shoot not sprout.
Like unripe grapes, he will be harvested before his time; he will be shaken off like the blossom of an olive tree.
For the testimony of the ungodly is death; fire will burn the houses of those who take bribes.
He will conceive pains; vain things will befall him; his belly will bear deceit.
Job speaks again in reply.
I have heard many such things. You are all comforters who bring misery.
Now, is there any order to words of wind? Or does someone trouble you to make you answer?
I too would speak to you if your soul were in the same condition as mine.
Then I too would sting you with words; I too would shake my head as you do.
Perhaps there would be strength in my mouth; I would not spare the movement of my lips.
For if I speak, the pains of my wounds will not subside; and if I remain silent, will I be any less wounded?
Now he has left me shattered, decayed, and numb; taking hold of me, he became a witness against me.
He raised my falsehood against me, for he answered against me.

Driven by anger, he destroyed me and gnashed his teeth at me. The arrows of his marauders rained down on me; he charged at me with the spearpoints of his eyes. Very swiftly he struck me on the knees; all together they raided me.
For the Lord handed me over to the unjust and cast me among the ungodly.
While I was at peace, he tore me apart; taking hold of my hair, he pulled it out. He set me up as a target.
Spears surrounded me; they mercilessly wounded my kidneys. He poured my bile onto the ground.
They shattered me with blow upon blow; mighty men rushed against me.
They sewed sackcloth onto my skin; my strength died out in the dust.
My belly burned from weeping, and the shadows of death lay upon my eyelids.
There was no injustice in my hands; my prayers were pure.
Earth, do not cover the blood of my body, and let there be no resting place for my cry.
And now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and my defender is on high.
May my petitions reach the Lord, and may my eyes shed tears before him.
Let a man plead his case before the Lord, and a son of man before his friend.
My numbered years have come to me; they have gone down a road with no return.
I perish, driven by the wind; I long for a grave but do not reach it.
I suffer, worn out, and what shall I do?
Strangers stole my possessions. Who is there who will clasp my hand?
For they hid their hearts from wisdom; therefore, do not exalt them.
Let him recount the evils in his portion; my eyes have wasted away over the children.
You made me a subject of slander among the nations; I became a laughingstock to them.
My eyes were blinded by anger, for I am hard pressed by everyone.
Amazement seized the upright at these things; the righteous will rise against the lawless.
The faithful will hold to his path, and the one whose hands are pure will gain courage.
But now, please, come and rise up, all of you, for I find no truth among you.
My days passed in pus; the veins of my heart burst.
They turned night into day; light drew near before the face of darkness.
For if I wait, the underworld is my home; my bed is spread in the gloom.
I called death my father, and the worm my mother and sister.
Now where is my hope? Or will I see my good fortune?
Or will they descend with me into the underworld? Or will we descend together into the dust?
Bildad the Shuhite speaks again in reply:
How long will you refuse to stop? Be quiet, so that we too may speak.
Why are we silent before you like four-footed animals, while you are consumed with anger?
But now, if you die, will everything under heaven remain uninhabited, or will the mountains be overturned from their foundations?
The light of the wicked will be extinguished, and no flame will reach them.
His light will become darkness in his house, and the lamp above him will be extinguished.
The lowliest will hunt down his possessions; his plans have gone astray.
His foot will fall into a snare, and he will become entangled in a trap.
Snares will come upon him; he will strengthen the thirsty against him.
For his nets are hidden in the earth, and his traps lie along his paths.
Many pains will destroy him on every side; they will surround his feet in the distress of hunger.
A terrible downfall is prepared for him; they will devour the [?] of his feet.
Untimely death will devour his beauty.
Healing will be driven from his house; a royal punishment will come upon him with anguish.
He will dwell in his house in his night; his beautiful things will be scattered with sulfur.
His roots will dry up below, and his crops will fall above.
His memory will perish from the earth, and his name will not be found in the world outside.
They will drive him from light into darkness, and let him have no acquaintance among his own people.
Let his household not survive under heaven; instead, strangers will dwell in what was his.
Those who come afterward will groan over him; astonishment seized those who came before.
For such are the houses of the unjust, and this is the place of those who do not know the Lord.
Job speaks again in reply.
How long will you torment my soul and shake me with words?
But know that the Lord has done this to me. You slander me and are not ashamed to attack me.
Yes, indeed, I have gone astray, and error has settled upon me: I have spoken words that are not fitting, and my words have gone astray and are not appropriate to the occasion.
Let us leave aside the fact that you have boasted against me and attacked me with reproaches.
Now know that it is the Lord who troubled me and raised fortifications against me.
Look, I am mocked with insults, yet I will not speak; I will cry out, but there is no justice anywhere.
I am hemmed in on every side and cannot pass through; he has put darkness over my face.
He stripped me of my glory and removed the crown from my head.
He surrounded me on every side, and I went away; he cut off my hope like a tree.
He treated me with fierce anger and considered me an enemy.
His bands of raiders came upon me together; those lying in ambush surrounded my paths.
My brothers have gone far from me; they acknowledged strangers rather than me.
My friends became merciless; those close to me despised me, and my acquaintances forgot my name.
The neighbors of my house and my maidservants considered me a stranger; I seemed a foreigner to them.
I called my servant, but he did not listen; my mouth pleaded.
And I begged my wife.
I called the sons of my concubines with coaxing words, but they disowned me forever; when I rise, they speak ill of me.
My acquaintances were disgusted with me, and those whom I loved rose against me.
My flesh has rotted along with my skin, and I hold my bones in my teeth.
Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, O friends, for the Lord’s hand has pierced me.
Why do you persecute me like the Lord? Are you not satisfied with my flesh?
Oh, that I could write down my words and put them in a book forever,
with an iron stylus in lead, or engraved on rocks.
For I know that the one who will deliver me on earth is everlasting,
to raise up my skin, which endured all this. This was brought upon me by the Lord.
This I know for myself; my own eye saw it, and no one else’s. Everything has come to an end within my bosom.
But if you say, “What shall we say before him, and shall we find the root of the matter in him?”
You too should fear what is hidden, for wrath will come upon the lawless, and then they will know where their substance is.
Zophar the Minaean speaks again:
I did not expect you to say this against us. Surely you are wiser than I?
I will listen to the instruction that humbles me, and a spirit of wisdom will give me an answer.
Have you known this only from now, or from the time when man was placed on the earth?
For the joy of the wicked is an overwhelming ruin, and the gladness of the lawless is destruction.
Even if his offerings rise to heaven and his sacrifices approach the clouds.
When he thinks he is secure, then he will perish completely, and those who knew him will say, “Where is he?”
Like a dream that has flown away, he will not be found; he has vanished like a vision in the night.
The eye that looked upon him will see him no more, and his own place will no longer recognize him.
Wicked men will destroy his children, and his hands will burn with pain.
His bones will be filled with his youth and will lie down with him in the dust.
If evil becomes sweet in his mouth, he will hide it beneath his tongue.
He will cherish it and not let it go, and will hold it within his throat.
And he will be unable to help himself; the gall of a viper is in his belly.
He will vomit up the wealth gathered through injustice; an angel will drag him out of his house.
He will suck the fury of dragons; the tongue of a serpent will kill him.
He will not see the milk of grazing herds, nor the pastures of honey and butter.
In vain and to no purpose he labored for wealth, of which he will not taste, like something hard that cannot be chewed or broken.
For he shattered the houses of many weak people, and seized dwellings rather than establishing them.
There is no deliverance for his possessions; amid his desires he will not survive.
There will be no stores of food for him; therefore his shoots will not flourish.
When he thinks, “Now I am full,” he will be distressed; every anguish will come upon him.
As for how his belly will be filled, he will send the fury of his anger upon him and cast pains upon him.
He will not escape the hand of iron; a bronze bow will wound him.
An arrow will pass through his body; stars will circle within his dwellings, and terrors will be upon him.
All darkness will await him; an unquenchable fire will devour him, and an intruder will afflict his house.
The heavens will reveal his lawlessness, and the earth will rise against him.
Destruction will utterly tear down his house; the day of wrath will come upon him.
This is the wicked man's portion from the Lord, and this is the inheritance of his possessions from the Visitor.
Job spoke again and said:
Listen, listen to my words! If only this consolation did not come from you!
Allow me, and I will speak, if you do not mock my words.
But now, are my complaints not against men? And why should I not be angry?
Look at me and be astonished, putting your hand to your chin.
If I remember, I will be distressed, for pains grip my body.
Why do the wicked remain alive at all, growing old and becoming great?
Their offspring are as they wish, and their children are before their eyes.
Their houses prosper, and there is no fear anywhere; punishment from the Lord is not upon them.
Their cattle do not fail to reproduce; their pregnant cows give birth safely and do not miscarry.
And they remain like everlasting flocks.
Their children play before them, taking up the psaltery and harp, and rejoice at the sound of songs.
They completed their lives in prosperity and peacefully fell asleep in the underworld.
And he says to the Lord, “Depart from me; I do not wish to know your ways.”
What gain is there in serving him, or what benefit is there in approaching him?
Good things were in their hands, and he does not look upon the deeds of the wicked.
Yet the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished; destruction will come upon him, and anguish will seize them because of wrath.
They will be like straw before the wind, or like dust carried away by a storm.
May his possessions consume his children; may he repay him and make him understand.
May his eyes see his own destruction, and may he not escape the Lord.
For his wishes are with him in his house, and they will divide the number of his months.
Is it not the Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge? For he himself examines the wise.
Such a man dies in the intensity of his folly, altogether prosperous and successful.
His belly is full of fat; his marrow will be moistened.
He will die in bitterness of soul, having eaten nothing good.
Together they will sleep in the earth; [?] covered them.
And now I know that you have come against me with insolence.
Now tell me: Where is the ruler’s house, and where is the dwelling place of the wicked?
Ask those who travel along the road, and do not disregard their signs.
For the wicked man is hurried toward the day of destruction; he will be led away on the day of his wrath.
Who will tell him to his face about his ways, and who will repay him for what he has done?
He went to the graves and kept watch in the tomb.
The gravel of the torrent bed became sweet to him. Everyone will go after him, and countless people have gone before him.
How can you comfort me with empty words? The semblance of relief means nothing to me.
Eliphaz the Temanite spoke again in reply:
Is it not the Lord who teaches wisdom and understanding?
Now, what concern is it to the Lord if you are blameless in your deeds? Or what benefit is it if you make your ways upright?
Will he take any account of you, rebuke you, and enter into judgment with you?
Is not your wickedness great, and are not your sins countless?
You took pledges from your brothers without cause and stripped the clothing from the naked.
You gave the thirsty no water to drink, and you even withheld bread from the hungry.
You showed partiality to certain people and settled them in the land.
You sent widows away empty-handed and tormented orphans.
And now snares have surrounded you, and an overwhelming conflict has thrown you into distress.
Your light turned to darkness for you, and water covered you in your sleep.
Does not the one who looks upon the heights see? Look, he humbled those clothed in pride.
And you said, ‘What does the Mighty One know? Can he judge through the mist?’
‘Clouds are his covering, and he will not be seen; he walks around the circuit of heaven.’
Will you keep to the age-old paths that righteous men tread,
who were snatched away before their time, their foundations a gushing river?
They said, ‘What will the Lord do to us, or what will the Almighty bring upon us?’
And he filled their houses with good things, but the counsel of the ungodly is far from him.
The righteous saw and laughed; the blameless man [?] scoffed.
Was not their firm foundation destroyed, and will not fire devour what remains of them?
But please be strong, if you are to endure and if your fruit is to be good.
Receive instruction from his mouth, and take his words into your heart.
And if you return and humble yourself before the Lord, remove injustice far from your dwelling.
You will dwell in the security of a rock, as on a rock in the valley of Ophir.
And the Almighty will help you against your enemies and make you pure like refined silver.
Then you will have confidence before the Lord, looking up to heaven with joy.
When you appeal to him, he will hear you and enable you to fulfill your vows.
He will restore to you a dwelling of righteousness, and there will be light on your paths.
For you humbled yourself and said, “I became arrogant”; and he will save those with downcast eyes.
And he will rescue the blameless person, and you will be saved through the purity of your hands.
Job speaks again in reply.
Indeed, I too know that my rebuke comes from my own hand, and his hand has weighed heavily upon my groaning.
But who can tell me whether I will find him and finally reach him?
I would present my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
I would learn the soothing words he would speak to me and understand what he would tell me.
And will he come against me with great power, or will he not carry out his punishment?
For truth and reproof come from him; he will bring my case to a complete conclusion.
If he goes ahead, I will no longer exist; and how can I know what comes afterward?
I did not grasp the left hand of the one who made him; and even if he were to cast his right hand around him, still I would not see.
For he knows my ways and has tested me like gold.
I will hold fast to his commandments; I will keep his ways and no longer turn aside.
I will not transgress his commandments, so that I may not die; I will hide his words in my heart.
But if he has judged in this way, who could oppose him? For he did whatever he himself wished.
Therefore I will hasten to him; having been instructed, I will attend to his concerns.
Because of these things, I will be troubled in his presence; I will reflect and be terrified of him.
For the Lord has weakened my heart, and the Almighty has troubled me.
For I did not know that darkness would come upon me; a mist covered what was before my face.
Why did the arrogant forget the Lord?
And the ungodly crossed the boundary and seized the flock together with its shepherds.
They drove away the orphan’s donkey and took the widow’s ox as a pledge.
They turned the weak away from the path of righteousness; together they drove the meek of the earth into hiding. They appeared like wild asses in the wilderness.
On my account they sold their labor; bread shared with the shameless became sweet to them.
They harvested an unripe field that was not theirs. The weak worked the vineyards of the ungodly without bread and without wages.
They made many lie down naked, without clothing; they stripped the clothes from their bodies.
They became wet from the dew of the mountains, and because they had no shelter, they placed themselves beneath a rock.
They snatched the orphan from the breast and afflicted the fallen.
They made the naked sleep without clothing; without cause they cut off bread from the hungry.
They lay in ambush in narrow places without cause; they did not know the paths of righteousness.
Those deprived of their cities and their homes—the souls of children—groaned deeply. And why would he not attend to this?
They were on earth and did not understand; they did not know the paths of righteousness and did not walk in his ways.
Knowing their deeds, he handed them over to darkness, and at night they will be like thieves.
The adulterer’s eyes will wait for darkness, and he will say, “No eye will see me.” And he put a veil over his face.
He dug through his house in the dark. By day they shut themselves in and did not know the light.
If morning for them is altogether in the shadows of death, if he takes to heart the terror of the shadows of death.
He is very light upon the surface of the waters. Their portion on earth will be destroyed; their planting will appear on the dry ground.
For they seized the orphan’s [?]. His sins were remembered against him; he vanished like a mist of dew.
He will be repaid for what he did; every unrighteous person will be broken like a tree that cannot be healed.
For he did no good to the barren woman and showed no mercy to the widow.
In anger he destroyed the weak, and even if he rises, let him not trust in his own life.
Let him become sick and not expect to recover, but fall through disease, for his arrogance has tormented many.
He will wither like a plant in the heat, or like an ear of grain falling from its stalk by itself.
But if there is anyone who says that I speak falsely, let him reduce my words to nothing.
Bildad the Shuhite speaks again:
Now, what sort of proverb is the fear that comes from him who makes everything in the heights?
Let no one think that there may be delay on the part of his troops. Upon whom will an ambush from him not come?
How can a person be righteous before the Lord, or who among those born of women can purify himself?
For if he commands the moon, it does not rise, and the stars are not pure before him.
Much less a human being, who is [?], and the son of man, who is a worm.
Job speaks again:
Whom will you approach, or whose helper will you be? Is it not the one whose strength is great and whose arm is mighty?
Whose counselor will you be? Is it not the one who has all wisdom? Whom will you follow, if not the one whose strength is great?
To whom have you spoken, and whose breath came out of you?
Can giants be born beneath the water and its neighboring regions?
The underworld is naked before him, and destruction has no covering.
He stretched out the north over nothing and hung the earth upon nothing.
He binds up the waters in his clouds, and the cloud is not torn beneath them.
He who holds the face of the throne spreads his cloud over it.
He encircled the surface of the waters with a command, as far as the boundary between light and darkness.
The pillars of heaven shook and were terrified at his rebuke.
By his strength he stilled the sea; by his wisdom the vast expanse is spread out.
The hosts of heaven trembled before him; by his command he killed the rebellious dragon.
Behold, this is part of his way, and we will still hear drops of his words from him. Who knows the power of his thunder when he brings it about?
Job again continued his discourse and said:
As the Lord lives, who has judged me in this way, and the Almighty, who has embittered my soul,
If my breath is still in me, and the spirit from God is around me, in my nostrils.
my lips will not speak lawlessness, nor will my soul contemplate injustice.
Far be it from me to call you righteous! Until I die, I will not give up my innocence.
I have held fast to righteousness and will not depart from it, for I am not aware of having done anything improper.
Yet even if my enemies were like the destruction of the ungodly, and those who rise up against me like the ruin of the lawless.
And what hope does the ungodly person have? Will he stand firm, trusting in the Lord? Will he perhaps be saved?
Or will the Lord hear his requests when distress comes upon him?
He will have no confidence before him; or, when he calls to him, will he listen to him?
But I will tell you what is in the Lord’s hand, and I will not lie about what is with the Almighty.
Look, you all know this. Why do you surround empty things with emptiness?
This is the wicked man’s portion from the Lord; the possession of the mighty will come upon him from the Almighty.
For even if many sons are born to him, they will be destined for slaughter; and if they reach young adulthood, they will wander as beggars.
Those who are with him will perish by death; let no one show mercy to their widows.
Even if he gathers silver like dust and stores up gold like clay,
the righteous will possess all of it, and the upright will take his wealth.
His house became like a moth and like a spider’s web.
The rich man lay down to sleep and will not rise again; he opened his eyes and will be no more.
Sorrows came upon him like water; darkness covered him in the night.
A scorching wind will carry him away, and he will depart; it will sweep him from his place.
He will cast him out and will not spare him; he will flee desperately from his hand.
He will clap his hands at him and drag him from his place.
For there is a place from which silver comes, and a place where gold is refined.
Iron comes from the earth, and copper is hewn like stone.
He set a limit to darkness, and he himself examines every boundary: stone, darkness, and the shadows of death.
A torrent’s ravine out of the dust; and those who forget the paths of righteousness will grow weak among men.
From the earth comes bread, and beneath it the earth was turned over as though by fire.
Its stones are a source of sapphires, and its soil is gold.
There is a path that no bird has known and that the vulture’s eye has not seen.
The sons of the proud have not trodden it, nor has a lion passed along it.
He stretched out his hand against the rock and overturned mountains from their foundations.
He cut open the winding courses of rivers; his eye saw every precious thing.
He revealed the depths of rivers and showed his power in the light.
But where is wisdom to be found, or where is the place of understanding?
No one knows its paths, and it is not found among human beings.
The depths said, “It is not with me,” and the sea said, “It is not with me.”
No pledge can be given in exchange for it, nor can silver be weighed out as its price.
It cannot be weighed against the gold of Ophir, precious onyx, or sapphire.
Gold and glass cannot be compared with it, nor can golden vessels serve as its price.
Heights and depths will not be mentioned, and he drew wisdom beyond the innermost things.
The topaz of Ethiopia cannot equal it; it cannot be weighed against pure gold.
But where is wisdom to be found, and where is the place of understanding?
It is hidden from human beings and concealed from the birds of heaven.
Destruction and death said, “We have heard of its glory.”
The Lord readily made its paths known, and he himself knows its place.
And he himself sees everything beneath heaven.
For he himself knows everything he made on earth: the weight of the wind and the measure of the waters that he made.
He himself saw and reckoned, and its path [?] as a voice rang out.
Then he saw it and spoke about it; having established it, he examined it.
And he said to humanity, “Look, worship of God is wisdom, and turning away from evil is understanding.”
Job again continued his parable and said:
“If only I could be as I was in the months of former days, when God guarded me,
when his lamp shone above my head, when I walked through darkness by his light,
when I was happy on my way, when the Lord watched over my house,
when I was clothed in greatness, and servants were around me,
When my paths were drenched with butter and my mountains were watered with milk.
when I went out into the city in the morning, and my seat was placed in the public squares.
Young men saw me and hid, and elders stood up.
Nobles stopped speaking and put their fingers over their mouths.
Those who heard about me called me blessed, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
For the ear that heard called me blessed, and the eye that saw recoiled from me.
For I rescued the poor from the hand of the powerful, and I helped the orphan who had no helper.
May the blessing of the one who was perishing come upon me, and the widow’s mouth blessed me.
I had clothed myself in righteousness and put on justice like a cloak.
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the weak, and I investigated cases I did not know.
I broke the jaws of the unjust and pulled their plunder from between their teeth.
I said, “Perhaps my life will reach old age, and I will live a long time like a palm tree.”
My root spread out over the waters, and dew will rest upon my harvests.
My hopes became vain to me; my tools and my bow passed into his hand.
When they heard me, they listened attentively and kept silent at my counsel.
They added nothing to my words; they were filled with joy when I spoke with them.
Like thirsty ground waiting for rain, they waited for my words.
If I laughed with them, they did not believe it, and the light of my face did not diminish.
I chose their way and sat as a ruler, and I lived like a king among soldiers, like one comforting others with tender care.
But now the lowliest laugh at me; now they admonish me together, those whose fathers I scorned, whom I did not consider equal to the dogs of my pastures.
And what use was the strength of their hands to me? Their end had perished upon them.
Barren through poverty and hunger, they fled yesterday from the waterless land, from distress and misery.
They surrounded themselves with rustling plants, and those very plants were their food.
They were dishonored and despised, lacking every good thing, and they chewed the roots of trees because of severe hunger.
Thieves rose against me, whose homes were holes in the rocks.
They will cry out amid the echoes, those who lived among wild thickets.
Children of fools and disgraced men, their glory extinguished from the earth.
Now I am their harp, and they make me a subject of slander.
They were disgusted with me and withdrew far away, and they did not refrain from spitting in my face.
For he opened his quiver and wounded me, and cast off the restraints from my face.
They rose up on the right of the branch; he stretched out his feet and made a path over me.
My paths were worn away along their paths of destruction; he stripped off my robe.
He wounded me with his arrows, approaching as he pleased.
I am afflicted with pain; pains have turned upon me. Hope has departed from me like the wind, and my deliverance like a mist.
And now my soul will be poured out within me; days of pain have taken hold of me.
At night my bones were seared, and my sinews have come loose.
With great force he seized my robe and surrounded me like the band of my robe.
He regards me as like clay; my portion is in dust and ashes.
I cried out to you, but you would not hear me; they stood and looked at me.
You met me without mercy; with a mighty hand you struck me.
You placed me in pain and cast me away from deliverance.
I know that death will destroy me, for the earth is the dwelling place of every mortal.
If only I could master myself, or plead with someone else and have him do this for me!
I wept over everyone who was weak, and groaned whenever I saw a man in distress.
I hoped for good, but behold, still more days of evil befell me.
My belly boils and will not cease; days of poverty have come upon me.
I will wander in distress without a muzzle; I stood in the assembly and raised a cry.
I became a brother to sirens and a companion to ostriches.
My skin has turned very black, and my bones are scorched by the heat.
My harp and my heart have turned to mourning, and my song to weeping.
I made a covenant with my eyes and did not look at a virgin.
And God allotted a portion from above, an inheritance from the Almighty on high.
Is there not destruction for the unjust, and exile for those who practice lawlessness?
Does he not himself see my ways, and will not all my steps be counted?
If I have walked with scoffers, if my foot has hurried toward deceit—
For I have been weighed in the scales of righteousness, and the Lord knows my innocence.
If my foot has strayed from the path, if my heart has followed my eye, if my hands have touched bribes—
Then let me sow and others eat, and let me be uprooted from the earth.
If my heart went after another man’s wife, if I lay in wait at the doors of his house,
then let my wife also please another man, and let my children suffer hardship.
For defiling a man’s wife provokes unbearable rage.
It is a fire burning in all his limbs; wherever it reaches, it tears everything out by the roots.
If I ever rejected the rights of a male or female slave who brought a case against me,
what shall I do if the Lord questions me? And if he visits me, what answer shall I give?
Did they not come into being in the womb just as I did? We came into being in the same womb.
As for the weak who were in need of something, did I ever turn them away? I did not make the widow’s eyes weep.
Did I ever eat my morsel alone and not offer any to the orphan?
For from my youth I raised him like a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided her.
Did I disregard a naked person who was perishing and fail to clothe him?
If the weak did not bless me, and their backs were warmed with the fleeces of my sheep,
if I raised my hand against an orphan, trusting that I had ample support,
then let my shoulder fall from its collarbone, and let my arm be broken at the elbow.
For fear of the Lord seized me, and I cannot remain calm before him.
If I laid up gold in my soil, if I trusted in precious stones,
if I rejoiced in the great wealth that came to me, if I laid my hand upon countless possessions,
or do we not see the shining sun grow dim and the moon wane, and not from them [?]?
If my heart was secretly deceived, if I put my hand to my mouth and kissed it,
then let that be counted against me as a great transgression, for I was false before the exalted Lord. From him come power and might, wisdom and understanding.
If I gloated over my enemy’s downfall and said in my heart, ‘Hurrah!’
then let my ear hear curses against me; then let me too become an object of disgust, reviled by my people.
If my maidservants often said of me, ‘Who would let us eat our fill of his flesh?’—for I was very sweet to them.
No stranger spent the night outside, for my door was open to everyone who came.
If I concealed my sins, having sinned unwillingly,
for I was not so ashamed before the great crowd that I would not tell them; if I ever let a weak person leave my doors empty-handed.
Who would grant me a hearing, if the Lord’s hand had not terrified me, or if the debt document I held against someone
were laid on my shoulders like a crown and read aloud?
And would I not tear it up and give it back, taking nothing from the debtor?
Has the earth ever groaned because of me, and have its furrows wept together?
And if I consumed its produce alone without paying, if I angered and distressed the owner of the land,
then let nettles grow instead of wheat, and brambles instead of barley. And Job ceased speaking.
Then his three friends also stopped speaking against Job, because Job was righteous in their eyes.
And Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Aram in the land of Uz, became angry. He was very angry with Job because he had presented himself as righteous before the Lord.
He was also very angry with the three friends because they could not give an answer against Job, yet declared him wicked.
And Elihu held back from answering Job because they were older than he was.
And Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouths of the three men, and his anger flared up.
Again Elihu, the son of Barachel the Buzite, said: “I am young in years, and you are older. Therefore I remained silent, afraid to tell you my own wisdom.
I said, ‘Those advanced in years should speak, and those with many years should know wisdom.’
But it is not so: there is a spirit in human beings, and it is the breath of the Almighty that teaches.
Those advanced in years are not necessarily wise, nor do the old know what is right.
Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me, and I will tell you what I know.’
Pay attention to my words. I will speak in your hearing until you examine the words,
so that I may understand [?]. And behold, there was no one among you who refuted Job and answered his words.
Do not say, ‘We have found wisdom by joining ourselves to the Lord.’”
And allow one man to speak such words.
They were dismayed and gave no further answer; they let their words grow old within them.
They remained silent and did not speak, for they stood there and gave no answer.
Again Elihu said: “I will speak once more.
For I am full of words, and the spirit within my belly is destroying me.
My belly boils like a tied wineskin of new wine, or like a blacksmith’s inflated bellows.
I will speak so that I may find relief, opening my lips.
I will not be ashamed before anyone, nor stand in awe of people.
For I do not know how to show partiality; otherwise a moth would devour me too.
But please, Job, hear my words and listen to what I say.
Look, I have opened my mouth, and my tongue has spoken.
My heart is pure in its words; the wisdom of my lips will be clearly understood.
It is the divine Spirit who made me, and the breath of the Almighty who teaches me.
If you can, give me an answer to this; otherwise, be silent.
Take your stand as I do, and I as you. You too are formed from clay; you and I alike were formed from the beginning.
Now, do not let fear of me terrify you, and do not let my hand weigh heavily upon you.
Nevertheless, you spoke in my hearing, and I heard the sound of your words.
For you said, ‘I am pure and have not sinned; I am blameless, for I have done no wrong.’
He found cause to blame me and considered me an adversary.
He put my feet in the stocks and watched all my paths.
How can you say, ‘I am righteous, and he did not listen to me’? For he who is above humanity is eternal.
And you say, ‘Why has he still not listened to every word in my case?’
The Lord will speak once, and a second time,
in a dream or in a nighttime meditation, when overwhelming terrors fall upon people as they slumber in bed.
Then people’s thoughts are revealed; with such a fearful vision he terrified them,
to turn a person away from wrongdoing, and he saved his body from destruction.
He spared his soul from death, so that he would not fall in battle.
Again he rebuked him with sickness in bed and numbed his many bones.
He will not be able to look forward to any food to eat, yet his soul will desire food.
Until his flesh rots away and his bones are exposed bare.
His soul drew near to death, and his life to the underworld.
If there are a thousand death-bringing angels, let not one of them wound him, if he resolves in his heart to turn to the Lord.
He will tell the man his wrongdoing and show him his foolishness; he will protect him from falling into death.
He will renew his body like plaster on a wall, and his bones will be filled with marrow. He will soften his body like a child’s and establish him, rejuvenated, among people.
When he pleads with the Lord, he will be accepted by him. He will enter with a composed face in confession, and he will render righteousness to people.
Then a person will reproach himself and say, ‘What things I did! Yet he did not punish me as I deserved for the sins I committed.’
He saved my soul from going into corruption, so that my life might see the light.
Look, the Mighty One does all these things in three ways with a man.
But he saved my soul from death, so that my life might bless him in the light.
Pay attention, Job, and listen to me. Be silent, and I will speak.
If you have something to say, answer me, for I want you to be justified.
But if not, listen to me. Be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.
Elihu spoke again:
Listen to me, you wise people; pay attention, you people of understanding.
For the ear tests words, and the throat tastes food.
Let us choose what is just for ourselves, and let us discern among ourselves what is good.
For Job said, 'I am righteous, and the Lord has cast aside my rights,
and he has falsified my judgment. My arrow is violent, though I have done no wrong.'
Who is like Job, who drinks contempt like water,
without sinning or acting wickedly or sharing the path of those who do lawless deeds by walking with the ungodly?
Do not say, 'A man is not called to account'; he is called to account by the Lord.
Therefore, you who have understanding in your hearts, listen to me. Far be it from me to act wickedly before the Lord or to disrupt justice before the Almighty.
Rather, he will repay a man according to each of his deeds, and he will find him on the man's own path.
Do you think that the Lord does anything disorderly, or that the Almighty perverts justice?
Who made the earth? Who is it who made what is beneath the heavens and everything in between?
If he wished to restrain it and keep the breath to himself,
all flesh would perish together, and all flesh would return to the dust from which it was created.
But if you are not instructed, listen to this; pay attention to the sound of my words.
If you do not consider the one who hates injustice and destroys the wicked, [?] the righteous live forever.
Wicked is the one who says to a king, 'You are unjust, more wicked than the princes,'
who did not show deference to honored persons and did not know how to give honor to men and show them favor.
Their crying out and pleading with others will be in vain, for they acted lawlessly to lead the weak astray.
For he himself sees the deeds of human beings, and nothing they have done is hidden from him.
And there is no place for those who commit lawlessness to hide.
For he will lay nothing further upon a man, since the Lord sees everyone.
He comprehends unsearchable, glorious, and wondrous things beyond number.
He knows their deeds and overturns them in the night, and they will be brought low.
He extinguished the ungodly; they were pointed out before their enemies.
For they turned aside from God's laws and did not acknowledge his judgments.
Thus they brought the cry of the needy to him, and he will hear the complaint of the poor.
If he himself grants silence, who will condemn him? And if he hides his face, who will see him?
Over nations and human beings alike he makes a hypocritical man king because of the people's harshness.
For someone says against the Almighty, “I took and seized without you.
If you have seen it, show me; and if I have done wrong, I will do it no more.”
Will anyone demand it from you because you reject it? You chose, not I; and if you know anything, speak.
Therefore those with understanding in their hearts will say this, and a wise man has heard this:
“But Job did not speak with wisdom, and his words lack understanding.”
Nevertheless, learn, Job, and do not give another answer like a fool.
Let us not add to your sins, nor let it be counted as lawlessness against you that you speak many words before the Lord.
Elihu spoke again:
“How did you consider that just? Who are you to say, ‘I am righteous before the Lord,’
or to say, ‘I have sinned; what shall I do?’
I will give an answer to you and to your three friends.
Look at the heavens and see; observe the clouds, how high they are above you.
If you have sinned, what will you do? And if you have committed many lawless deeds, what can you do?
But if you are righteous, what will you give him, or what will he receive from your hands?”
Your wickedness concerns a man like you, and your righteousness a son of man.
Those slandered by the multitude will cry out; they will cry out because of the power of the many.
And no one said, “Where is God, who made this?”
Who keeps the watches of the night, who distinguishes me from the four-footed animals of the earth and from the birds of heaven.
There they will cry out, but he will not listen, because that happening comes from the arrogance of the wicked.
For the Lord does not wish to see disorder, for the Almighty himself sees those who commit lawlessness, and he will save me.
Plead your case before him, if you can praise him as he is.
And now, because there is no one who has borne his anger, and no one who fully knows his own transgressions.
So Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words in ignorance.
Elihu speaks again:
Wait for me a little longer, so that I may teach you, for I still have words within me,
having brought my understanding from afar.
Through deeds I will speak truthfully of my rights, and not unjust words conceived without cause.
Know that the Lord does not reject the innocent; he is mighty in strength.
He will not keep the heart of the wicked alive, and he will give justice to the poor.
He will not turn his eyes away from the righteous. The one found before him is with kings on a throne, and he will seat them forever, and they will be exalted.
And the wicked, bound with shackles, will be entangled in the nets of poverty.
He will tell them of their deeds and their transgressions, that they have grown strong.
And he will listen to the righteous one and tell them to turn away from injustice.
If they listen and serve him, they will complete their days in prosperity and their years in delight.
But he will not keep the wicked alive, because they did not wish to acknowledge the Lord, and because they were admonished and were disobedient.
Those who are hypocritical at heart will provoke anger; they will not cry out, because he has bound them.
Their soul will die in youth, and their life will be wounded by angels,
because they oppressed the weak and powerless. He will bring forth justice for the meek, and he rescued you from the mouth of the enemy.
The depths, whose expanse is beneath them; and your table came down full of rich food.
May the rights of the righteous not fail; may anger come upon the wicked,
because of the wickedness of the bribes they received unjustly.
Do not let willful thoughts about petitions lead you astray when the weak are in distress.
And do not draw out all the mighty by force at night, for peoples to rise in their place.
But be careful lest you do what is improper, for you rescued him from poverty.
Behold, the Mighty One will strengthen by his power, for who is mighty like him?
Or who examines his works? Or who will say, “The deeds he did were unjust”?
Remember that his works are great, which righteous men began.
Every person has seen for himself how wounded people are.
Behold, the Mighty One is great, and we cannot know the number of his endless years.
The drops of rain are counted by him, and they will pour as rain into the clouds.

The aged ones will pour forth. He made the clouds shade countless people; they spread mist over many people. He set a time for the animals, and they know the order of birth. At all this, will your mind not be astonished? Will your heart not tremble within your body? For he did great things that we did not know. He commands the snow, “Be upon the earth,” and gives the winter rains their strength. He sets a seal on the hand of every person, so that every person may know his own weakness.
Do you understand the spreading of the clouds, the evenness of his tent?
Behold, he stretches out over it along a path, and he has covered the roots of the sea.
For by these he will judge the peoples; he will give food to the one who has grown strong.
He hid the light in his hands and gave orders for it to strike.
He will tell his friends about it, about his possessions, and about injustice.
And at this my heart was troubled and flowed from its place.
Listen to the sound of the Lord’s furious wrath, and counsel will come from his mouth.
His dominion is beneath all the heavens, and his light is over the ends of the earth.
After it a voice will cry out; he will thunder with his lofty voice, and he will not change them, for he will make his voice heard.
And the Mighty One will thunder with his wondrous voice, for he did great things that we did not know.
He commands the snow, saying, “Be on the earth,” and the winter rains according to their strength.
He sets a seal on the hand of every person, so that every person may know his own weakness.
Wild animals went into their resting places and hid in their lairs.
Dew comes out of the storehouses, and cold from the heights.
And from the breath of the Mighty One he will give frost; he changes the waters as he wishes.
