And he will scatter the chosen cloud; mist scatters his light, and he himself turns the circles.
He placed their work wherever he wished, and everything he commands them—these things are appointed by him upon the earth.
Whether for correction, or for his earth, or for mercy, they will find him.
Listen to this, Job; stand still and reflect on the Lord’s power.
We know that God established his works; he made light in darkness.
He knows the examination of the clouds; the transgressions of evildoers are terrifying.
And your warm robe rests quietly upon the earth.
Will you make things firm with him from the south, strengthening them for ages, like the appearance of frost?
But why, indeed? Please teach me what we should say to him, and let us stop speaking at length.
Is there a book or a scribe standing near me, so that I may silence men in writing?
Light is not visible to everyone; it shines in ancient times [?], like the light from him upon the clouds.
From the north comes a cloud gleaming with gold; above these things, great are the glory and honor of the Almighty.
And we find no other like him in power. He judges the righteous; do you not think you should listen to him?
Therefore people will fear him; those who are wise in heart will also fear him.
After Elihu had finished speaking, the Lord spoke to Job from the whirlwind and the cloud.
Who is this who hides his plans from me, gathering words in his heart and thinking he can hide them from me?
Gird your waist like a man. I will question you, and you must answer me.
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if you have understanding.
Who determined its measurements, if you know? Or who stretched a measuring line over it?
On what were its foundations secured? Who laid its cornerstone?
When the ancient stars came into being, all the angels of the stars blessed me with a loud voice, and all my angels praised me.
I shut in the sea with doors when it was born, coming out of its mother's womb.
I gave it clouds as clothing and mist as swaddling bands.
I set boundaries for it, putting bars and doors in place.
I said, ‘You shall come this far and go no farther; here your waves shall break against you.’
Was it in your time that I summoned the morning light, and the morning star saw its appointed place,
to reach over the wings of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
Or did you take clay from the soil and fashion a living creature, and place it on the earth able to speak?
Did you withhold light from the wicked and break the arms of the arrogant?
Have you reached the source of the sea and walked along the paths of the depths?
Will the gates of death open for you in fear? Will the gatekeepers of Hades tremble when they see you?
Do you understand the breadth of what lies beneath these heavens? Come, tell me how great it is.
What is the land where light dwells, and what is the place of darkness?
Will you take me to their boundaries, if you know their paths?
Perhaps you know, since you were born at that very time and the number of your days is great.
Have you entered the storehouses of snow, and have you seen the treasuries of hail?
Has it been stored up for you for times of enemies, for a day of battle and war?
Where does the frost come from, or where is the south wind scattered beneath heaven?
Who prepared the rushing torrents of rain and the paths of thunder, pouring rain upon the earth
where there is no one, in an uninhabited wilderness,
to satisfy the untrodden and uninhabited land and make green plants spring up?
Who is the father of rain, and who gave birth to the drops of dew?
From whose womb does ice come forth, and who gave birth to the frost in heaven,
which descends like flowing water? And who melted the face of the heavens?
Do you understand the arrangement of the Pleiades, and have you opened the barrier of Orion?
Or will you open Mazzaroth in its season, and will you lead the Evening Star by its hair along with them?
Do you know the circuits of the heavens, or all the things that exist beneath heaven?
Will you call to the cloud with your voice, and will it obey you with trembling, full of abundant water?
Will you send out lightning bolts, and will they go and say to you, ‘What is it?’
Who gave women wisdom in weaving or skill in embroidery?
Who counts the clouds with wisdom and has bent the heavens down to the earth?
And it lies poured out like dusty earth, and I have bound it together like a block of stone.
Will you hunt food for lions and satisfy the appetites of dragons?
They tremble in their dens and sit in ambush in the woods.
Who prepared food for the ravens? For their young cried out to the Lord and wander about seeking food.
Do you know the time when the wild goats of the caves give birth? Will you watch over the birth pangs of deer?
Will you count all the months until they give birth? Will you release them from their labor pains?
Will you raise their young without fear? Will you drive their labor pains away from them?
Their young become free and increase in number as they are born; they go out and do not return.
Who set the wild donkey free? Who loosened its bonds?
I made the wilderness its dwelling and the salt flats its home.
It laughs at crowded cities and does not listen to the tax collectors’ reproaches.
It surveys the mountains where it grazes and roams in search of every green thing.
Will the unicorn be willing to serve you or rest beside your manger?
Will you bind a yoke to it with harness straps, or will it draw a furrow in your field?
Will you rely on it because its strength is great, and will you leave all your work to it?
Will you trust it to return your seed to you and gather the produce of your threshing floor?
The wings of the flying [?]—will the [?] and the [?] conceive?
For it lays its eggs on the ground and warms them in the soil.
And it forgets that a foot may scatter them and that the wild beasts of the wilderness may trample them.
It treats its young as strangers, as though they were not its own; it has labored in vain, without fear.
For God has silenced wisdom within it and given it no share in understanding.
When it rises to the heights, it laughs at the horse and its rider.
Did you give the horse strength and clothe its neck with armor?
Did you put armor on it and make boldness the glory of its chest?
It thunders in the field and strikes with its hoof; it goes out into the field with strength.
When it encounters arrows, it scorns them and does not turn back from iron.
Above it flash the bow and sword, with the shaking of shield and spear.
In its fury it tears up the earth, and it does not believe until the trumpet sounds.
When the trumpet sounds, it cries, “Ha! Ha!” From far away it catches the scent of battle, running and snorting.
Is it by your wisdom that the hawk stands with its wings spread, looking motionlessly toward the south?
Or is it at your command that the eagle and the vulture rise above their nest?
They sit and rest in rocky caves and hidden places.
There they remain and seek food; their eyes watch from far away.
Its young are drenched in blood; wherever there is a carcass, they are found there at once.
And the Lord God answered Job and said:
“Will anyone distort the judgment of the Almighty, rebuke God, and give him an answer?”
Job spoke again to the Lord:
“Why should I still argue, rebuked and reproved by the Lord? I hear such words, for I am nothing. What answer can I give to this, except to put my hand over my mouth?
I have spoken once, and I will not add a second time.”
Again the Lord speaks once more to Job from the cloud.
“Not so! Instead, brace your waist like a man. I will question you, and you give me an answer.
Do not reject my judgment, and do not suppose that the revelation announced to you had any other purpose than that you might appear righteous.
Is your arm equal to the Lord’s arm? Can you thunder with a voice like his?
Come now, take on majesty and power, and clothe yourself in glory and honor.
Send forth angels in anger, humble all the proud, and extinguish the arrogant.
Make the ungodly rot at once,
and bury them all together in the earth, out in the open, and fill their faces with disgrace.
Then will I acknowledge that your right hand is able to save?
But this is before you: the beasts feed on grass like cattle.
Look, its strength is in its waist, and its power is in the navel of its belly.
It raises its tail like a cypress; its sinews are intertwined.
Its ribs are bronze, and its backbone is cast iron.
It is the first of the Lord’s creatures, made as a plaything for his angels.
Coming upon the rocky slope of a mountain, it brought joy to the four-footed creatures in Tartarus.
It sleeps beneath various kinds of trees, among papyrus, reeds, and rushes.
Great trees shade him, together with the woods and the branches of the chaste tree.
If a flood comes, it does not notice; it is confident even if the Jordan rushes into its mouth.
It will receive it into its eye sockets. As it escapes, will you pierce its nostrils?
Will you draw up the dragon with a hook? Will you put a muzzle around its snout?
Will you fasten a ring in its nose? Will you pass a bit through its jaws?
Will he speak to you gently and with a soft voice?
Will he make a covenant with you? Will you subdue him as a servant forever?
Will you play with him as with a bird, and tie him with a cord like a fledgling?
Will nations feed on him, and will the peoples of the Phoenicians divide him among themselves?
All the vessels gathered together cannot lift a single scale from his tail, nor carry his skull into fishermen’s boats.
Lay your hand on him, remembering the battle that will take place in his body, so that it will not happen again.
Have you not seen him, and will you not marvel at these words that have been spoken?
Are you not afraid, since he is prepared even for me? But who is there who will stand against me?
Or who is there who will turn against me and endure, since everything under heaven is mine?
I will not be silent about him, and the word of the Mighty One will have mercy on his equal.
Who will strip away the covering of his face, and who will enter the folds of his armor?
Who will open the doors of his face? Terror surrounds his teeth.
His belly consists of bronze shields; his joints are like emery stone.
One is joined behind another, and no air can pass through.
Each follows after its brother; they hold on to one another and do not separate.
Flashes of light burst from his sneezing; his eyes look like the morning star.
Blazing torches come from his mouth, and sparks of fire burst out and fall.
From his nostrils rises the smoke of a furnace of fiery sparks.
His breath is sparks, and flame comes out of his mouth.
Strength dwells in his neck; destruction runs before him.
The parts of his body are firmly joined; even if something is poured upon him, they will not move.
For his heart is hardened like stone, and stands firm like a blacksmith’s immovable anvil.
When he moves, terror falls upon the wild beasts, the four-footed animals, and the creeping creatures of the earth.
If spears strike him, weapons and lances have no effect.
For he considers iron straw, and bronze like rotten wood.
A bronze bow does not wound him; he considers a sling stone grass.
Hammers were reckoned by him as reeds; he mocks the fiery trembling.
His bedding is sharpened spears; all the gold of the sea beneath him is like boundless mud.
He makes the depths boil like a pot; he regards the sea as nothing.
He reckoned the Tartarus of the depths as a single captive, and the abysses as his walking ground.
There is nothing on earth like him, made as a plaything for my angels.
He sees everything lofty, and he is king of all that are in the waters.
Job again speaks to the Lord:
I know that you can do everything, and nothing is too difficult for you.
Who is it who hides counsel from you, thinking to conceal it by holding back words? Who will tell me what I did not know, the great and marvelous things that I did not understand?
Now listen to me, Lord, so that I too may speak. I will question you, and you teach me.
Previously I heard of you by the hearing of my ears, but now my own eye has seen you.
Therefore I rejected myself and melted away, and I consider myself dust and ashes.
After the Lord had spoken these words to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “You and your two friends have sinned, for you have spoken nothing true before me as my servant Job has.

But now take seven young bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job. He will offer burnt offerings for you, and my servant Job will pray for you. For if I had not regarded him, and if it were not for him, I would already have destroyed you, because you did not speak the truth about my servant Job.”
Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Minaean went and did as the Lord commanded them, and he forgave their sins for Job’s sake.
The Lord increased Job’s prosperity, and when he prayed for his friends, he forgave their sins. The Lord gave Job twice as much wealth as he had before.

All his brothers and sisters heard of everything that had happened to him and came to him. All who had known him before ate and drank with him, comforted him, and marveled at everything the Lord had brought upon him. Each gave him one ewe and one unstamped gold coin worth four drachmas.
The Lord blessed Job’s latter days more than his former days. His livestock consisted of fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand grazing female donkeys.
Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
He named the first Day, the second Cassia, and the third Horn of Amalthea.
No women more beautiful than Job’s daughters were found under heaven, and he gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.

Job lived for a hundred and seventy years after his afflictions, and all the years he lived were two hundred and forty-eight. Job saw his children and his children’s children to the fourth generation.

Job died old and full of days. It is written that he will rise with those whom the Lord raises. This is translated from the Syriac book. He lived in the land of Uz, on the borders of the Edomites and the Arabs. His former name was Jobab. He married an Arabian woman and fathered a son whose name was Ennon. His father was Zerah, the son of Esau’s son, and his mother was a woman of Bozrah, so that he was the fifth generation from Abraham. These are the kings who reigned in Edom: first, Balak son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dinhabah. After Balak came Jobab, who was called Job. After him came Asom, who was a military commander in the land of the Temanites. After him came Hadad son of Barad, who slaughtered Midian in the plain of Moab, and the name of his city was Getham. The friends who came to him were Eliphaz, of the descendants of Esau, king of the Temanites; Bildad, ruler of the Shuhites; and Zophar, king of the Minaeans.
